title: Uses of Dimensional Analysis & Its Limitations
notes: Dimensional analysis is used in three ways. It checks whether an equation could be right. It converts a numerical value from one unit system to another. It suggests the form of a relation when the relevant quantities are known.
To find a form, write the unknown as a product of powers of the chosen quantities, then equate the powers of M, L and T on both sides. The solution of those three equations gives the powers.

The time period of a simple pendulum is assumed to depend on its length and on g, and not on the mass, when the amplitude is small. Matching dimensions then gives T proportional to the square root of l/g.
The method cannot produce the 2π in that pendulum formula. Any dimensionless constant is invisible. An experiment, or a full derivation, has to supply it.

The method also fails if a needed quantity is left out of the assumption, or if too many quantities are included. With more than three unknown powers and only M, L and T, the powers are not fixed uniquely.
Trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions accept only dimensionless inputs. Dimensional analysis will reject a formula that puts a length alone inside a sine.

exercises.question: Assume the period of a simple pendulum depends on length l and g as T = k l^a g^b. Find a and b.
steps: Mass does not appear, which matches the assumption.
For length: 0 = a + b, so a = 1/2.
Therefore T = k sqrt(l/g). Dimensions do not give the value of k.
exercises.answer: a = 1/2, b = -1/2, so T is proportional to sqrt(l/g).
